title: Natural transport of lisse fibres along etale paths
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ be prime, and let $X$ be a nonempty connected smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For a geometric point $a$ let $F_a$ be the finite-etale fibre functor of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. An etale path $p:a\rightsquigarrow b$ means a natural isomorphism $F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}F_b$. Paths exist between any two geometric points of $X$.

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Every path $p$ induces natural $E$-linear isomorphisms
$$p_L:L_a\xrightarrow{\sim}L_b$$
for lisse $E$-sheaves $L$ of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. On an integral model this is the inverse limit of its maps on the finite locally constant $R/\varpi^r$-module stalks, followed by inversion of $\varpi$. It agrees, under the lisse realization and point-fibre comparison of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], with transport on the ordinary pro-etale lisse module sheaf. Thus the assertion applies also to framework lisse objects and the point fibres $\operatorname{Fib}_s(La^*L)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] (in degree zero, with the analogous interpretation at arbitrary geometric points).

These maps preserve identities and composition of paths and satisfy $p_{L'}u_a=u_b p_L$ for every sheaf map $u:L\to L'$. They commute with finite coefficient extension $E\subset E'$ and with scalar extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ at a common finite stage. For a scheme automorphism $h:X\to X$, not necessarily $k$-linear, the path $h(p):h(a)\rightsquigarrow h(b)$ obtained by evaluating $p$ on $h^*$ satisfies
$$p_{h^*L}=(h(p))_L$$
under the canonical pullback-stalk identifications. The same assertion holds for iterates of $h$. On geometric loops the maps are exactly the actions of $\pi_1(X,a)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_a)$ in [cor-galois-lisse-representations]; in particular
$$p_L\rho_a(\delta)p_L^{-1}=\rho_b(p\delta p^{-1}).$$

source.place: Tag 0BND, pione-theorem-fundamental-group (2); module and adic extension: Deligne, literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf (1.1.1), (1.1.6), pp. 146-150; ordinary pro-etale realization: literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Proposition 6.8.4, Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10. The explicit compatibility package is an agent formulation of these fibre constructions.

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is connected, so [lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport] gives a natural isomorphism between the fibre functors on finite locally constant sheaves of sets at $a$ and $b$. The fibre-compatible equivalence [thm-galois-lc-etale] identifies these with the finite-etale fibre functors, giving the required path. Conversely, any given path $p$ on finite etale covers extends to finite locally constant set sheaves through this equivalence. Explicitly choose $M\cong h_P$ and conjugate $p_P$ by the stalk maps. Full faithfulness makes the result independent of the presentation: a second presentation gives an isomorphism of covers, and the equality is the naturality square for that isomorphism. Thus $p$ defines a natural family of bijections $p_M:M_a\to M_b$. The following steps spell out the compatibility formulas and the additional pro-etale/framework and automorphism assertions.

source.place: Tag 0BND, pione-theorem-fundamental-group (2), and Tag 03RV, etale-cohomology-lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; explicit functorial construction.

proof.text: Let $M$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of modules over a finite ring $A$. Fibre functors preserve finite limits by [thm-galois-fundamental], so the map on $M\times M$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(p_Mx,p_My)$, as follows by composing with both projections. Naturality for addition, zero, and the endomorphism given by each $c\in A$ shows $p_M(x+y)=p_Mx+p_My$, $p_M0=0$ and $p_M(cx)=cp_Mx$. Thus $p_M$ is $A$-linear, with inverse induced by $p^{-1}$. Naturality for every module-sheaf map is the underlying set-sheaf naturality. On a constant finite sheaf $S$, every $s\in S$ comes from a map from the terminal sheaf, so naturality fixes $s$; hence $p_S=1$.

source.place: Tag 0BND, pione-theorem-fundamental-group (2), and Tag 03RV, etale-cohomology-lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; explicit functorial construction.

proof.text: For a homomorphism $A\to B$ of finite rings, use the stalk/scalar-extension isomorphism of [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension](3). For each $c\in B$, the map of underlying finite locally constant sheaves $M\to B\otimes_A M$, $m\mapsto c\otimes m$, is a set-sheaf map. Naturality from step 1 gives $p_{B\otimes_A M}(c\otimes m)=c\otimes p_M(m)$. Pure tensors generate the stalk module and step 2 gives additivity, so $p_{B\otimes_A M}=1\otimes p_M$. The same formula twice proves compatibility with composites of coefficient homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0BND, pione-theorem-fundamental-group (2), and Tag 03RV, etale-cohomology-lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; explicit functorial construction.

proof.text: For a lisse integral model $\mathcal M=(M_r,t_r)$, apply step 2 to each $M_r$ and naturality to every $t_r$. It gives a well-defined $R$-linear bijection $p_{\mathcal M}:(m_r)_r\mapsto(p_{M_r}(m_r))_r$ between inverse-limit fibres, with coordinatewise inverse. These are precisely the fibres of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Define $p_L=p_{\mathcal M}\otimes_R E$ on $L=\mathcal M\otimes E$. A morphism in this rational category is a finite sum of tensors $u\otimes c$ of integral morphisms and scalars; the equality for $u$ at each level gives the equality for $u\otimes c$ by $E$-linearity. Thus the construction is a natural isomorphism on the rationalized category, including isomorphisms between different models. The reconstruction of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1) ensures the integral fibres are finitely generated and complete. Identities and composites are preserved because every coordinate has these properties; this also proves the corresponding equalities after localization.

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147; fibre/representation convention (1.1.6); coordinatewise argument.

proof.text: For $E\subset E'$ use the scalar-extension construction of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](3): its level $m$ is scalar extension of level $\lceil m/e\rceil$, where $e$ is the ramification index. Step 3 identifies the path map on this level with $1\otimes p_{M_{\lceil m/e\rceil}}$. The fibre/scalar identifications supplied by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) are compatible with those finite reductions; completeness and the reconstruction isomorphisms of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] therefore identify the limit map with the scalar extension of $p_{\mathcal M}$, and after inverting uniformizers identify it with $p_L\otimes_E E'$. Equality can be checked after every finite reduction, so the result also respects successive extensions. In the common-finite-stage category of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](4), represent two objects and a morphism over one common finite field. The just-proved compatibility makes transport independent of enlarging that field. Extending its vector-space fibres to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ gives the asserted algebraically closed coefficient compatibility.

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147; fibre/representation convention (1.1.6); coordinatewise argument.

proof.text: For a scheme automorphism $h$, let $\tau_{a,P}:F_a(h^*P)\cong F_{h(a)}(P)$ be the canonical pullback-fibre bijection of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and similarly at $b$. Define $h(p)_P=\tau_{b,P}\,p_{h^*P}\,\tau_{a,P}^{-1}$. Naturality of $\tau$ and $p$ makes this a path. Under the base-change-compatible equivalence [thm-galois-lc-etale], precisely this formula holds for underlying finite module sheaves. Thus $\tau_b p_{h^*M}=h(p)_M\tau_a$ at each finite coefficient level. Apply the coordinatewise limits and scalar localizations of steps 4-5 to get $p_{h^*L}=(h(p))_L$ under the canonical fibre identifications. Iterating this equation gives the assertion for every nonnegative iterate, and applying it to $h^{-1}$ gives negative iterates. The finite-cover bijections come from the fibre-product projections and their composites, so their composition identifications agree. Nothing here assumes $h$ is $k$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0BND, pione-theorem-fundamental-group (2), and Tag 03RV, etale-cohomology-lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; explicit functorial construction.

proof.text: For a loop $\delta\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_a)$, [cor-galois-lisse-representations] specifies its action on every finite coefficient sheaf to be evaluation of that natural automorphism on the underlying finite locally constant set sheaf. This is exactly step 2 applied to $\delta$; its adic action is specified to be the same action at every finite level. Consequently the rational transport for $\delta$ is $\rho_a(\delta)$. Evaluate the composite natural automorphism $p\delta p^{-1}$ on each finite sheaf: its value is $p_M\delta_Mp_M^{-1}$. Step 4 preserves composition and inverses, so passing to limits and localizing gives $\rho_b(p\delta p^{-1})=p_L\rho_a(\delta)p_L^{-1}$.

source.place: (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147; fibre/representation convention (1.1.6); coordinatewise argument.

proof.text: To compare with ordinary pro-etale sheaves, first replace a classical rational lisse sheaf by a finite-free integral model. Under [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) it corresponds to a finite-dimensional continuous $E$-representation of the profinite group $\pi_1(X,a)$. The stable lattice of [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] is finite free, and its finite reductions give a lisse integral sheaf by the integral equivalence in that same corollary. After rationalization this sheaf is isomorphic to the original one. Step 4 already proves naturality for this isomorphism, so this replacement does not change transport. The argument includes a zero-dimensional representation and does not assume the initially chosen integral model is torsion-free.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10; explicit comparisons as specified in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-smooth-lisse-integral-lattice] with $K_0=K=k$ and $T_0=X$ (the identity field extension). It supplies a globally lisse finite-free completed-integral lattice for every ordinary pro-etale lisse $E_X$-module. The scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. It is separated by hypothesis, and $\ell$ is invertible. Thus [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] applies: reduction identifies these lattices with the finite-free etale towers, and rational realization is fully faithful. Use steps 1-4 on that tower to define ordinary lisse transport. If two lattices realize isomorphic rational objects, full faithfulness expresses their comparison as a rationalized integral morphism, and step 4 intertwines it; hence the result is independent of the lattice. The pullback and coefficient comparisons in that node are induced by the same finite-level maps, so steps 3, 5 and 6 give their compatibilities. Step 8 shows that for every classical rational lisse sheaf its realization has exactly the transport constructed above.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10; explicit comparisons as specified in the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: For a geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, the pullback compatibility of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] identifies the pulled-back integral lattice with the inverse limit of the pulled-back finite etale tower. By [thm-galois-lc-etale] and [lem-galois-geometric-fibre], a pulled-back finite locally constant sheaf is the constant sheaf of its fibre at $x$. Sections of this inverse limit are the inverse limit of the finite fibres, because limits of sheaves are computed on sections. The reconstructed module is finite free; its associated completed coefficient-module sheaf and its localization give respectively the same integral and rational point fibres. The path map on them is therefore exactly $(m_r)\mapsto(p_{M_r}m_r)$ followed by inversion of $\varpi$. This uses pullback compatibility for lisse towers, not commutation of arbitrary stalks with infinite limits. Finally [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies framework lisse objects, ordinary module pullbacks, finite coefficient extension and the point fibres $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lx^*L)$ for $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, naturally in maps. Conjugating our transport by these specified point comparisons proves the framework assertions, including $h$ and its iterates; the preceding tower description is the analogous interpretation at arbitrary geometric points.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-68601e121 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 10 steps in full, plus the statement of every cited node. Sources checked at the cited places: Stacks 0BND(2) in pione.tex (an isomorphism between fibre functors exists), Bhatt-Scholze Prop 6.8.4(1),(4) and Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, and Weil II (1.1.1). Step-by-step: (1) path existence comes from lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport, which needs only connectedness, and thm-galois-lc-etale moves it to finite etale covers. (2) Linearity follows from thm-galois-fundamental's compatibility with finite limits and from naturality for addition, zero and multiplication by scalars; this is genuinely elementary. (3) Finite scalar extension uses clause (3) of lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension on pure tensors. (4) The integral transport is built level by level, then inverting the uniformizer gives the rational one; torsion integral models are covered. (5) Coefficient extension uses the level ceil(m/e) and the reconstruction results of lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules. (6) For an automorphism h, the fibre bijection tau comes from lem-galois-pi1-functoriality, which allows any morphism, so h need not be k-linear. I checked the orientation: tau_b p_{h*L} = h(p)_L tau_a. Negative iterates come from h^{-1}. (7) The loop action and the conjugation formula follow from the cor-galois-lisse-representations normalization. (8) A free stable lattice exists because pi_1 is profinite and the action is jointly continuous. (9) The global lattice comes from lem-a1 with K_0=K=k. Its hypotheses hold, as do the Noetherian and separated hypotheses of lem-per (X is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian); full faithfulness then makes the transport independent of the lattice. (10) At an arbitrary geometric point the fibre is computed through the pullback of the finite tower; the framework comparison of lem-tw is applied only at s=Spec k, which matches the statement's own scope. Edge cases checked: X a point, identity and inverse paths, rank 0, torsion models, ramified E'/E, negative iterates. There are no new nodes. The overlap with lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport is partial: that node lacks the h-pullback equation and the pro-etale/framework comparison, so the item is not a duplicate. Batch-5 check: the closures of lem-a1 (reaching lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal through algebraic spaces and descent), lem-per (reaching the general definition def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves), lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules, lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension and lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice contain only general foundations. None of them states the trace formula or Poincare duality or is a cohomological step of their proofs, and the item is not a step of either proof, so all five are accepted (the unit sk-p-real-operations also lists sec-poincare-duality in its uses). All 13 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes. No fixes.
